recurring_harms: harm falling on people who are not the paying user;dignity and autonomy loss from being represented or judged without consent;misinformation presented with the confidence of a trusted source;privacy loss from sensitive or biometric data retained beyond its purpose;financial or opportunity loss the affected person cannot appeal
human_in_loop_decisions: All three industries share the same rule: a human must hold the decision where the outcome is hard to reverse for a specific person. Rejecting a candidate, acting on a clinical suggestion, and publishing synthetic speech in a real person's voice all require a named reviewer with time, the underlying evidence, authority to override, and an appeal path for the affected person. A reviewer who only sees a recommendation and an accept button is a rubber stamp, not a control.
strongest_guardrails: Refuse rather than degrade: the system blocks the irreversible action when a precondition is unmet, instead of proceeding with a warning. Concretely, no output without a stored consent or eligibility artifact, one hundred per cent provenance or decision-record coverage as a hard limit never traded against volume, evidenced deletion for sensitive data, and a guardrail breach that pauses onboarding rather than opening a backlog item.
cross_industry_pattern: Across the three industries the failure rarely starts in the model. It starts in governance, where consent, eligibility or scope was never verified, and in the user experience, where the safe path costs the user more effort than the unsafe one. That changes the release roadmap in one specific way: verification and disclosure gates move ahead of model quality work, because a better model does not fix an unverified consent artifact or a publish flow whose default is silence. It also means the release gate belongs on evidence of the control working, not on the control existing. Support for this pattern is strongest in the content-creator evidence collected here and weaker for the other two industries, which the group discussed from the case starters rather than from its own source review, so this is a working hypothesis rather than a validated finding.
